html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Compare ephemeral and persistent storage and the common volume types
  • Explain PersistentVolumes, claims and binding
  • Use StorageClasses, access modes and reclaim policies in a scenario
  • Describe CSI, expansion, snapshots and StatefulSet storage

2Ephemeral versus persistent storage, volume types (emptyDir, hostPath, local, configMap, secret, projected)

Running case

Harbor Books Keeps Its Data

  • The postgres database holds every order, so its data must survive when its Pod is replaced or moves to another node
  • The cache only needs scratch space that can disappear with its Pod
  • The platform team wants storage to be created on demand, not by hand for each request
  • In this module you give each part the right kind of storage

Volumes: Ephemeral and Persistent

  • A container's own filesystem is ephemeral: after a crash the container comes back with a clean state
  • A volume is a directory that the containers of a Pod can use and share
  • Ephemeral volumes are created and deleted with the Pod
  • Persistent volumes have a lifecycle independent of any Pod, so the data stays when the Pod moves

Exam tip

Ask how long the data must live: the container, the Pod, or longer.

Common Volume Types

Volume What it gives the Pod
emptyDir scratch space that starts empty once the Pod has a node; shared by its containers; deleted with the Pod, but safe across container crashes
hostPath a file or directory from the node's filesystem; many security risks, so avoid it
local a disk, partition or directory on a node, used as a static PersistentVolume
configMap, secret files filled from a ConfigMap or a Secret
projected several sources mapped into one directory, all from the Pod's namespace
persistentVolumeClaim the way a Pod uses a PersistentVolume
Exam tip

An emptyDir lives and dies with its Pod; avoid hostPath.

3PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, binding, using a claim

PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim

  • A PersistentVolume (PV) is storage that the cluster offers, with a lifecycle independent of any Pod
  • A PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is a user's request for storage: a size and access modes
  • A control loop binds each claim to a matching PV, one to one
  • With no matching PV, the claim stays unbound until one appears

Exam tip

Pods use claims; claims bind volumes.

Using a Claim

  • The claim asks for a size, access modes and, optionally, a StorageClass
  • A Pod uses it with persistentVolumeClaim and a claimName in its volumes
  • The claim and the Pod must share a namespace
  • A claim that a Pod is using is protected from immediate removal

A claim for the postgres data

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: postgres-data
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: standard
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
Exam tip

The Pod names the claim, in its own namespace.

4StorageClass and dynamic provisioning, binding mode

StorageClass and Dynamic Provisioning

  • A StorageClass describes a class of storage: a provisioner, parameters and a reclaimPolicy
  • Dynamic provisioning creates a volume on demand when a claim asks for it, so nobody pre-creates PVs
  • A claim with no storageClassName gets the default StorageClass
  • WaitForFirstConsumer waits until a Pod uses the claim; the default mode is Immediate

Exam tip

Claim in, StorageClass decides, PV out.

5Access modes and reclaim policy

Access Modes and Reclaim Policy

Access mode Short What it allows
ReadWriteOnce RWO read-write by a single node
ReadOnlyMany ROX read-only by many nodes
ReadWriteMany RWX read-write by many nodes
ReadWriteOncePod RWOP read-write by a single Pod in the whole cluster
  • Retain: when the claim is deleted, the PV is Released and keeps its data until an administrator reclaims it
  • Delete: the volume is deleted with the claim; a dynamically provisioned volume follows its StorageClass, which defaults to Delete
  • Recycle is deprecated
Exam tip

RWO is per node, RWOP is per Pod; Retain keeps data, Delete removes it.

6CSI, volume expansion, snapshots, StatefulSet storage, storage types and Rook

CSI, Expansion and Snapshots

  • CSI (Container Storage Interface) is a standard interface for exposing storage systems to containers
  • A vendor ships a driver that is built outside the Kubernetes code base, unlike the older in-tree plugins
  • Expansion: edit the PVC to ask for more storage, if its StorageClass sets allowVolumeExpansion
  • Snapshots: a VolumeSnapshot requests a snapshot of a volume; it is a CRD and needs a CSI driver

Exam tip

CSI is the standard plug-in interface for storage drivers.

StatefulSet Storage and Storage Types Beyond the curriculum

Storage type In Kubernetes
File a filesystem mounted into a directory: the default Filesystem volume mode
Block a raw device with no filesystem (volumeMode: Block); the application must handle it
  • A StatefulSet uses volumeClaimTemplates to give each replica its own claim
  • Those claims stay when the Pods or the StatefulSet go away: remove them by hand, unless a retention policy says otherwise
  • Rook, a CNCF graduated project, orchestrates Ceph, which offers file, block and object storage
Exam tip

A StatefulSet's claims outlive its Pods.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A container in a Pod with an emptyDir volume crashes and is restarted. Later the Pod is removed from its node. What happens to the files in the emptyDir?

  • AThey are lost at the crash, because an emptyDir belongs to the container and not to the Pod
  • BThey survive the crash, and they are deleted permanently when the Pod is removed from the node
  • CThey survive both the crash and the removal, because an emptyDir is a persistent kind of storage
  • DThey are copied to a PersistentVolume when the Pod is removed, so that the Pod can resume later
Show the answer

Answer: B. An emptyDir is created once the Pod has a node. A crashing container does not remove the Pod, so the data survives the restart, but it is deleted permanently when the Pod is removed from the node.

S2The Harbor Books postgres Pod must keep its data when it is replaced and started on another node. Which object does the team create to ask for that storage?

  • AA PersistentVolume that names the postgres Pod as its owner, created by the Pod itself
  • BAn emptyDir volume in the Pod spec, sized large enough for the whole database
  • CA hostPath volume that points at a folder on the node where the Pod started first
  • DA PersistentVolumeClaim with a size and access mode, which the Pod uses by name
Show the answer

Answer: D. A claim requests persistent storage, and the Pod uses it by name, so the data stays when the Pod moves. An emptyDir is deleted with the Pod, a hostPath ties the data to one node, and a PV is not owned by a Pod.

S3A PersistentVolumeClaim names no storageClassName, and the cluster has a default StorageClass. What happens?

  • AThe default class is used, and a volume is provisioned on demand for the claim
  • BThe claim is rejected, because every claim must name a StorageClass of its own
  • CThe claim waits until an administrator creates a matching PersistentVolume by hand
  • DThe claim is bound to the oldest PersistentVolume, whatever its size or access mode
Show the answer

Answer: A. A claim with no class gets the default StorageClass, and dynamic provisioning then creates a matching volume on demand. Nobody has to pre-create a PV, and binding always matches size and access modes.

S4Which access mode lets only one Pod in the whole cluster mount a volume read-write?

  • AReadWriteOnce, because it allows one Pod to use the volume at a time
  • BReadOnlyMany, because many nodes may mount the volume, and they may read from it
  • CReadWriteOncePod, because it limits read-write use to a single Pod
  • DReadWriteMany, because many nodes may mount the volume for reading and writing
Show the answer

Answer: C. ReadWriteOncePod allows read-write use by a single Pod across the whole cluster. ReadWriteOnce is per node, so several Pods on that node can still use the volume.

S5Harbor Books deletes the claim of a test database, and the reclaim policy of the bound PersistentVolume is Retain. What happens to the volume and its data?

  • AThe volume is deleted at once, together with the data on the underlying storage
  • BThe volume stays in the Released phase, and its data is kept until an administrator reclaims it
  • CThe volume binds to the next claim that asks for storage, after its old data is erased first
  • DThe volume is scrubbed with a basic wipe and becomes Available again for a new claim
Show the answer

Answer: B. Retain allows manual reclamation: the PV is Released and keeps its data. Delete would remove the volume, and Recycle, the basic scrub, is deprecated.

S6What does the Container Storage Interface (CSI) make possible?

  • AStorage vendors can add a driver for their system without changing the Kubernetes code base
  • BPods can share the network namespace of the node that runs them, for faster storage access
  • CContainer images can be built inside the cluster and pushed to a registry in one step
  • DAdministrators can pin Pods to nodes that hold the right disks, with no scheduler involved
Show the answer

Answer: A. CSI is a standard interface between Kubernetes and storage systems, and drivers live outside the Kubernetes code base. It has nothing to do with node networking, image builds or scheduling.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Lifetimes container filesystem, emptyDir with the Pod, PersistentVolume beyond the Pod
Claims a PVC requests storage, a control loop binds it to one PV, and the Pod names the claim in its own namespace
StorageClass provisioner, parameters and reclaim policy; dynamic provisioning creates volumes on demand; the default class fills in for a claim with no class
Modes and reclaim RWO per node, RWOP per Pod; Retain keeps the data, Delete removes it
CSI the standard driver interface, with expansion and snapshots
StatefulSet one claim per replica, kept when Pods go
